title: Declare behaviour in htmx markup with hx-on/hx-trigger, not inline on<event> handlers

values: edited file contains at least one hx- attribute
facts.note: Sole scope gate: content-level check on any non-test file regardless of extension or rendering mechanism (HTML, templates, JSX, etc.). The htmx_hypermedia_detector already performs this self-scoping check; activation needs a content observer exposing it.

fires: Editing any non-test file containing an hx- attribute, even if it currently has no inline handlers (preventative guidance before one is introduced)
Editing a template with an hx-get element and adding onclick="…" to it
A file containing any hx- attribute also contains onsubmit="…" or onchange="…" on any element
A JSX file that contains an hx- attribute and a lowercase onclick="…" attribute
doesNotFire: A plain HTML page with no hx- attribute that uses onclick="…"

given: A non-test file of any kind (HTML, template, JSX, …) contains at least one `hx-` attribute
when: You add or change element behaviour in that file
then: Use no lowercase inline handler (`on<event>="…"`, e.g. onclick/onsubmit/onchange); declare behaviour with `hx-on` or `hx-trigger`.
prefer: `<button hx-get="/rows/1" hx-on::after-request="track('open')">Open</button>` instead of `<button hx-get="/rows/1" onclick="track('open')">Open</button>` (dies on swap).
`hx-on` for element-scoped behaviour, `hx-trigger` for the request itself; both survive swaps because htmx re-processes new content.
Presentational, non-request behaviour: a delegated listener on a stable ancestor that is never swapped.
avoid: Any lowercase `on<event>="…"` (onclick, onsubmit, onchange, …) in htmx-driven markup.
Mixing the two models: each inline handler is behaviour invisible to the hypermedia lifecycle; they accumulate and drift the codebase back to a JS layer.
unless: The file contains no `hx-` attribute (self-scoping; never scanned).
React/JSX camelCase props (`onClick={…}`, `onSubmit={…}`): different mechanism, out of scope. Only these props are exempt, not JSX files as such.
why: Swapping an element destroys its inline handler and any closed-over state; conversely a swapped-OUT element's handler can stay live on a detached node, firing stale clicks on markup the user can no longer see. hx-on/hx-trigger join htmx's event and swap lifecycle.
evidence: htmx_hypermedia_detector reports no lowercase `on<event>="` attribute in any non-test file containing an `hx-` attribute.
Reviewer confirms behaviour previously in inline handlers is expressed via hx-on/hx-trigger or a delegated listener on a never-swapped stable ancestor.
verifier_detail: Detector: zero-dependency Bun implementation (htmx_hypermedia_detector, validator). Step 1: confirm the file contains an `hx-` attribute; otherwise skip the file entirely (self-scoping). Step 2: flag any lowercase `on<event>="` attribute in it. No file-extension gate.

Matching is deliberately lowercase-only so React camelCase JSX props like `onClick={…}` (different mechanism, different lifecycle semantics) are never flagged; lowercase `onclick="…"` inside an hx-bearing JSX file IS flagged.
Term htmx_driven_markup: a file that contains at least one `hx-` attribute. Term inline_event_handler: a lowercase HTML attribute of the form `on<event>="…"` carrying JavaScript in markup.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic "behaviour is declared where the framework can see it" obligation, enforced by the htmx_hypermedia_detector family implementation on atdd.workspace.bun.
Source name: "htmx-driven markup declares behaviour with hx-attributes, not inline handlers"; summary: a "no inline JS handlers in hypermedia markup" obligation.

sharedNodes.text: strict: atdd-bun fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
